data.name: Giridhar
data.long_meaning: Giridhar is a Sanskrit name derived from two roots - 'Giri' meaning mountain and 'Dhar' meaning to bear. The name signifies one who bears the mountain, a powerful and majestic figure. In Hindu mythology, this name is associated with Lord Vishnu who is often depicted as Giridhar, carrying the mountain Meru on his back.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, stability, and divine protection.

Giridhar may serve as a strong inspiration for individuals who seek to carry the weight of responsibilities on their shoulders, much like Lord Vishnu. It is also a reminder of the various deities and heroes in Hindu mythology, who are revered for their ability to bear heavy burdens.

The name also emphasizes on the idea of inner strength and resilience to bear the weight of life's challenges. It serves to inspire individuals to draw upon their inner strengths and remember the divine presence within them during times of struggle. Additionally, the name reminds individuals of their connection to the natural world, signifying survival and perseverance in the face of adversity.
